summary: Provides up to 6 months of rental assistance that may be used for:   Rental arrears (overdue rent)  Current month's rent  Up to one month of future rent   Rental assistance applicants may also apply for utility assistance for current and past-due bills from Denver Water and/or Xcel Energy as well as relocation assistance if eviction cannot be prevented.

fields.service summary: Provides up to 6 months of rental assistance that may be used for:   Rental arrears (overdue rent)  Current month's rent  Up to one month of future rent   Rental assistance applicants may also apply for utility assistance for current and past-due bills from Denver Water and/or Xcel Energy as well as relocation assistance if eviction cannot be prevented.
fields.eligibility: Applicants must:   Be aged 18 and older  Have a Demand for Rent of Possession from their landlord or have an active Forcible Entry and Detainer (FED) eviction case  Have a household income at or below 80% of the Area Median Income (AMI)  Reside in the service area   Additional eligibility requirements may apply. Area Served: City and County of Denver
fields.access method: Visit the website to apply during the application window. Call or text for more information or technical assistance.
fields.required documents: Must provide:   Copy of current Demand for Rent or Possession or eviction notice  Evidence of financial hardship (or other housing crisis) which may be in the form of self-attestation within the online application  Evidence of rent due, which may be in the form of:  A signed lease agreement  Demand or eviction notice  Tenant ledger  Past payment receipts    Evidence of tenancy, which may be in the form of a signed lease agreement or an official document showing the tenant's name and address, such as a:  Driver's license  Pay stubs  Rent ledger  Utility bill    Photo identification  Proof of income for each household member aged 18 years or older, which may be in the form of:  Bank statements  Pay stubs  Tax returns (most recent filing)
fields.hours of operation: Monday - Friday, 8:30 a.m. - 5:30 p.m. (CARE Center); October 20th, 2026, Tuesday, 10 a.m. - October 21st, 2026, Wednesday, 9:59 a.m. (Application Window)

fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Statewide
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable

title: Eviction Prevention Assistance - Before Court Summons — Community Economic Defense Project — 1600 N Downing St - Denver County
summary: Provides emergency financial assistance through a monthly random selection process for households with qualifying eviction documents, including those in the early stages of the eviction process. Assistance may include past-due rent, future rent, eligible fees, and relocation costs when necessary to prevent displacement.

fields.program name: Eviction Prevention Assistance - Before Court Summons
fields.physical address: 1600 N Downing St, Ste 600, Denver, CO, 80218
fields.detailed services: Specialized Information and Referral; Rent Payment Assistance; Eviction Prevention Assistance
fields.service summary: Provides emergency financial assistance through a monthly random selection process for households with qualifying eviction documents, including those in the early stages of the eviction process. Assistance may include past-due rent, future rent, eligible fees, and relocation costs when necessary to prevent displacement.
fields.eligibility: Applicants must:   Be in the early stages of the eviction process  Be aged 18 years and older  Have a household income at or below 60% of the Area Median Income (AMI)  Be at risk of eviction or displacement  Have one of the following active eviction documents:   Demand for Rent  Mediation documentation  Payment plan documentation established under House Bill 25-1168  Court summons  Eviction notice  Stipulation agreement  Writ of restitution  Sheriff's notice    Have established residency at the rental property before applying  Have made at least one rent payment  Not have received Emergency Rental Assistance Program assistance from any Colorado Emergency Rental Assistance Program agency within the previous 24 months  Not have exceeded the program maximum of seven months of assistance or $10,000 in prior assistance   Additional eligibility requirements may apply. Area Served: Statewide
fields.access method: Visit the website during the monthly pre-application window to submit a pre-application.
fields.required documents: Applicants must provide:   One of the following active eviction documents:  Demand for rent  Payment plan documentation established under House Bill 25-1168  Mediation documentation  Court summons  Eviction notice (if this is a separate court document used by the program)  Stipulation agreement  Writ of restitution  Sheriff's notice    Proof of residency at the property for which assistance is requested. Documentation may include:  Executed lease signed by the tenant and landlord or property manager  Other written document naming the applicant as a tenant  Driver's license or other government-issued ID showing the property address  Income documents showing the applicant's name and property address  Current utility bill or other official mail addressed to the applicant at the property    Proof of the rent amount due. Documentation may include:  Lease or other written rental agreement showing the rent amount and due date    Proof that annual household income is at or below 60% of the Area Median Income (AMI)   If the applicant is not listed on the lease, they must also provide proof of at least one rent payment made during the month immediately before the month assistance is requested. Documentation may include:   Copy of a check  Receipt for a cash payment or affidavit from the property owner  Payment record from Venmo, PayPal, or another financial institution  Receipt for a money order or cashier's check
fields.hours of operation: October 13th, 2026, Tuesday, 10 a.m. - October 15th, 2026, Thursday, 5 p.m. (Monthly Pre-Application Window); Monday - Friday, 9 a.m. - 12 p.m.; 1 p.m. - 4 p.m. (Administrative Hours); Monday - Friday, 8:30 a.m. - 5:30 p.m. (CARE Center Hours)
